title: Feedback
log: 2026-11-01T14:46:41Z match: Claude Haiku 5.5 found no bank point the same, so it is written new
2026-11-02T04:41:51Z recheck: the fresh check agreed with the fix, cleared with the fix

match.reason: The closest bank card covers internal and external feedback and its focus on results or movement, but it does not teach the brief's point that too much feedback can make a learner dependent on it, so a new point is needed.

draft.title: Feedback
card: information the learner senses from their own body during or after a movement, such as the feel of a ball leaving the hand.
information from a source outside the learner, such as a coach's comment, a video replay or a scoreboard.
Feedback can be about the result of the action, such as the distance a throw travelled. It can also be about the movement itself, such as the position of the elbow during the throw.
Feedback helps a learner improve. Too much can make a learner depend on it, so they struggle to judge their own movement when it is not given.
draft.remember: Feedback guides learning, but too much can leave the learner leaning on it.

a.q: A swimmer watches a video replay of her freestyle stroke with her coach. What type of feedback is the replay?
opts: External feedback about the movement
Internal feedback about the movement
External feedback about the result
Internal feedback about the result
a.why: A video comes from outside the swimmer, so it is external. It shows how the stroke looks, so it is about the movement. It is not about the result, which would be her time or place.
a.clue: Ask where the information comes from, then what it describes.

b.q: Coach Dan tells a junior golfer what to fix after every swing, and the golfer now looks to him before each shot. What is the most likely problem?
opts: The golfer depends on feedback and cannot judge own swing
The golfer gets too little external feedback to improve
The golfer ignores internal feedback because it is wrong
The golfer only receives feedback about the result
b.why: Constant feedback can make a learner rely on the coach. The golfer then struggles to sense and fix their own swing. Too little feedback is not the issue here, since Dan gives it after every swing.
b.clue: Think about what happens when the coach is not there.

b.best: The golfer depends on feedback and cannot judge own swing

problems.detail: The right option drops a word ('cannot judge own swing' should read 'their own swing'). It also says 'cannot', which is stronger than the card's 'struggle to judge their own movement'. Suggest 'The golfer depends on feedback and struggles to judge their own swing'.

check.summary: The card and both questions are accurate. Question b's right option has a missing word and says 'cannot' where the card says 'struggle', so it needs a small rewording.
